details: Bitcoin continues to face significant price volatility, struggling to maintain levels above $60,000. Macroeconomic pressures, including hotter US inflation and broader equities sell-offs, coupled with substantial institutional withdrawals from Bitcoin ETFs totaling $2.6 billion in November, are driving the downturn and challenging year-end recovery hopes.
title: Bitcoin volatility persists, ETF outflows hit $2.6B in November.

details: Galaxy Digital has withdrawn its October assessment that Bitcoin's bear market had concluded in June. Alex Thorn, Galaxy's head of research, indicated that a daily close below $58,525 could trigger further declines, with a potential target around $48,500 based on historical patterns.
title: Galaxy retracts Bitcoin bear market end call, eyes $48.5K.

details: Ethereum remains under pressure, trading below $1,700 as US spot ETH ETFs recorded approximately $64.1 million in net outflows on Tuesday, contributing to a total of about $1.22 billion in withdrawals for November. This persistent institutional selling, alongside broader inflation concerns, continues to hinder ETH's recovery prospects.
title: Ethereum ETFs see $1.2B November outflows, ETH below $1,700.

details: Fidelity has submitted an S-1 filing with the SEC for a spot Chainlink (LINK) ETF (ticker FLNK, Nasdaq), designed to track LINK's price without staking. This development is seen as a significant step towards expanding institutional investment opportunities in altcoins beyond just Bitcoin and Ethereum.
title: Fidelity files for spot Chainlink ETF, boosting altcoin institutional access.

details: Ukraine's parliament passed a Virtual Assets Bill, aiming to align with EU MiCA regulations and implement a 5% tax on crypto profits. Concurrently, South Korea's FSC unveiled its Digital Asset Basic Act, which includes provisions for won-backed stablecoins and exchange ownership rules, signaling a global trend towards increased regulatory clarity in the crypto space.
title: Ukraine legalizes crypto, South Korea proposes digital asset act.

details: Renowned chart analyst Peter Brandt has issued a serious warning, suggesting that Ethereum (ETH) could experience a significant crash to $500. This potential 71% drop from its current price comes after a difficult month for ETH, although a specific timeline for this prediction was not provided.
title: Veteran trader Peter Brandt warns Ethereum could crash to $500.
